_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2023: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2022 state of the verified 2022 register (its one 2022 change — China's ~3% objective of 5 Mar 2022 — is the starting CN row, and its general note is carried unchanged), updated for the 2023 current-year targets set earlier: Brazil 3.50 → 3.25% ±1.5 (CMN Res. 4,831 of 25 Jun 2020, art. 1; DOU 26 Jun 2020); Indonesia 3% ±1 (PMK 101/PMK.010/2021, Art. 2(3)(b)); Thailand 2.0, the midpoint of the 1–3% headline range approved by the Cabinet on 27 Dec 2022 (THE STANDARD and The Nation the same day, which the row's wording quotes; the BoT announcement No. 1/2565, dated 30 Dec 2022, is a scanned PDF read from the page images and is cited only from its file's creation on 3 Jan 2023, its unofficial English translation only from that file's creation on 20 Feb 2023); Türkiye 5% ±2pp, the 'medium-term' target maintained (CBRT Monetary Policy and Liraization Strategy for 2023, 30 Dec 2022, paras 49–51; the Turkish and English PDFs were both created that day and last modified 4 Apr 2023); Colombia 3% (Board of 25 Nov 2022, 'reitera la meta de inflación del 3%'; no range restated; banrep.gov.co sits behind a bot check, so the release's text was read from the site's print rendering at www.banrep.gov.co and its date taken from Valora Analitik's same-day report, which quotes it). Korea's 2% (26 Dec 2018, no fixed period) is carried: the BoK's Review on Inflation Targeting Operations of 20 Dec 2022 (Governor Rhee's remarks, BIS reprint) refers to 'the inflation target of 2%' and changed nothing. India's 4% is carried. Changes announced during 2023: China's Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2023 (CPI 'around 3%', value unchanged; recorded as the new year's objective; applies from 2023-03-12); New Zealand's new Remit issued 26 Jun 2023 after the first five-yearly review (Gazette notice and the Minister's release 27 Jun, in effect 28 Jun; 'achieve and maintain' rather than 'keep' 1–3%, house prices moved to a redrafted context section; value unchanged, wording replaced; applies from 2023-07-02); Australia's new Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy of 8 Dec 2023 (2–3%, with policy set so that inflation returns to the midpoint; value unchanged, wording replaced; applies from 2023-12-17); New Zealand's amended Remit announced 13 Dec 2023 with the Economic Objective Amendment Bill (the Gazette notice of 20 Dec says it was issued 12 Dec and took effect 20 Dec, the day after Royal assent; 1–3% with a focus on the 2% mid-point kept, maximum sustainable employment removed; value unchanged, wording replaced; applies from 2023-12-17). The RBNZ website refused access (HTTP 403), so neither remit's own text was read: both are quoted from the Minister's and the Reserve Bank's releases (Mirage News and Scoop reprints of the same day), the Gazette notices and RNZ. Value-unchanged reaffirmations are not recorded: the FOMC's reaffirmation effective 31 Jan 2023; the UK remit of 22 Nov 2023 ('the operational target for monetary policy remains an inflation rate of 2%'); the BoJ's decision of 28 Apr 2023 to conduct a broad-perspective review (2% target unchanged); the new Sveriges Riksbank Act in force from 1 Jan 2023 (the CPIF 2% specification applies until further notice; no new specification was proposed); the Brazilian CMN of 29 Jun 2023 (3.25% for the year kept); India's MPC resolutions; the Colombian Board of 30 Nov 2023 reiterating 3%. Targets set during 2023 for later years are not recorded (Brazil's CMN of 29 Jun 2023, a continuous 3% target from 2025; Thailand's Cabinet approval of the 2024 target of 26 Dec 2023; the CBRT's Monetary Policy for 2024 of 29 Dec 2023, 5% medium-term target kept), nor is anything announced after the last edition's cutoff of 30 Dec 2023. The ECB, Norges Bank, MNB, CNB, NBP, Banxico, SARB, RBI, SNB and Banco Central de Chile targets are unchanged (checked against December 2023 or other 2023 publications, mostly through search results); Canada's 2021 framework runs for five years from 2022 and nothing changed in 2023. Not cited: the Bangkok Post (paywall) and the Thai Cabinet's own summary on thaigov.go.th (HTTP 400). Every new source was fetched and its quoted text checked; sources are shown only once published; no wording names a later year.
note: Where an official objective refers to an index other than headline CPI (the Federal Reserve's PCE price index; see each row), the benchmark is applied to headline CPI. India's benchmark is the RBI's stated CPI objective for the current period. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective from its Report on the Work of the Government (until that report, the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area, the ECB's symmetric 2% target. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: FOMC Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy as amended 27 Aug 2020: the longer-run goal of 2 percent PCE inflation is kept, and the Committee 'seeks to achieve inflation that averages 2 percent over time', so that 'following periods when inflation has been running persistently below 2 percent, appropriate monetary policy will likely aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time' (value unchanged).
US.index: PCE price index; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Federal Reserve press release, 'Federal Open Market Committee announces approval of updates to its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy', 27 Aug 2020

XM.wording: ECB strategy review, 8 Jul 2021: 'The Governing Council considers that price stability is best maintained by aiming for a 2% inflation target over the medium term. This target is symmetric, meaning negative and positive deviations of inflation from the target are equally undesirable' (replacing 'below, but close to, 2%'; HICP remains the measure).

urls.label: ECB press release, 'ECB's Governing Council approves its new monetary policy strategy', 8 Jul 2021

JP.wording: 'The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy', 22 Jan 2013: 'the Bank sets the "price stability target" at 2 percent in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index (CPI)' (replacing the 1% 'price stability goal' of February 2012); in the joint statement with the Government the Bank will 'aim to achieve this target at the earliest possible time'.

urls.label: Bank of Japan, The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 22 Jan 2013
Joint Statement of the Government and the Bank of Japan on Overcoming Deflation and Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth, 22 Jan 2013

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

urls.label: HM Treasury, Budget 2010 (June, HC 61), 22 Jun 2010, para 1.27

CA.wording: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework, 13 Dec 2021: 'The target will continue to be defined in terms of the 12-month rate of change in the total CPI. The inflation target will continue to be the 2 percent mid-point of the 1 to 3 percent inflation-control range'; the agreement runs for another five-year period, beginning with 2022. 'The primary objective of monetary policy is to maintain low, stable inflation over time'; monetary policy 'should continue to support maximum sustainable employment', and the Bank 'will continue to use the flexibility of the 1 to 3 percent control range to actively seek the maximum sustainable level of employment when conditions warrant' (value unchanged).

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework, 13 Dec 2021

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016: 'They agree that an appropriate goal is to keep consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over time' (midpoint 2.5%; the previous Statement said 'over the cycle').

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: Riksbank, 7 Sep 2017: 'The Executive Board of the Riksbank has decided to adopt inflation measured in terms of the CPIF (the consumer price index with a fixed interest rate) as a formal target variable for monetary policy. The target for monetary policy is that the annual change in the CPIF shall be 2 per cent, that is, the same level previously applied to the CPI'; a variation band of 1–3 per cent replaces the ±1pp tolerance band, applying from the monetary policy decision of 6 Sep 2017.
SE.index: CPIF (CPI with a fixed interest rate); benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Sveriges Riksbank press release No. 21, 'CPIF target variable for monetary policy', 7 Sep 2017

NO.wording: Regulation on Monetary Policy laid down by the Government on 2 Mar 2018 (in force immediately; the 2001 regulation repealed from the same date), Section 3: 'The operational target of monetary policy shall be annual consumer price inflation of close to 2 percent over time. Inflation targeting shall be forward-looking and flexible so that it can contribute to high and stable output and employment and to counteracting the build-up of financial imbalances.' Norges Bank: 'The inflation target is now 2%, compared with the previous 2.5%.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 1/18, 15 Mar 2018 (reproduces the Regulation of 2 March 2018 on Monetary Policy, p. 13)
Norges Bank, Executive Board's assessment, Monetary Policy Report 1/18, 15 Mar 2018

NZ.wording: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Replacement of Remit for Monetary Policy Committee) Order 2021 (LI 2021/29, made 22 Feb 2021, notified 25 Feb 2021): the inflation objective is unchanged — 'keep future annual inflation between 1 and 3 percent over the medium term, with a focus on keeping future inflation near the 2 percent mid-point' — and the Committee shall, in pursuing its operational objectives, 'assess the effect of its monetary policy decisions on the Government's policy [to support more sustainable house prices]' (value unchanged; recorded because the remit is replaced).

urls.label: New Zealand Gazette, notice 2021-dl640: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Replacement of Remit for Monetary Policy Committee) Order 2021, LI 2021/29, 25 Feb 2021

CN.wording: Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2022, main projected targets for development this year: a CPI increase of around 3 percent ('今年发展主要预期目标是：…居民消费价格涨幅3%左右'; CGTN: 'keeping the CPI increase – the main gauge for inflation – at around 3 percent'; a government objective, not a PBoC target; the previous year's was also around 3%).

IN.wording: On 31 Mar 2021 the Government retained the CPI inflation target at 4 per cent with lower and upper tolerance levels of 2 and 6 per cent for the next five years, from April 2021 (value unchanged; recorded because the statutory target was re-notified); the MPC's resolutions keep setting policy 'in consonance with the objective of achieving the medium-term target for consumer price index (CPI) inflation of 4 per cent within a band of +/- 2 per cent'.

(um e meio ponto percentual) e de mais 1,50 p.p. (um e meio ponto percentual)' (3.25% with a ±1.5pp tolerance band).

TR.wording: Medium-term CPI inflation target of 5%, set jointly with the Government: the CBRT's Monetary Policy and Liraization Strategy for 2023 (30 Dec 2022; the renamed successor of the annual Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy text), para 49: 'Hükümet ile birlikte belirlenen orta vadeli enflasyon hedefi yüzde 5 olarak korunmuştur' ('The medium-term inflation target of 5% set jointly with the Government has been maintained'); para 50: 'While converging to the medium-term inflation target, the targets announced via Inflation Reports will serve as interim targets and a reference to inflation expectations.' Para 51: the uncertainty band 'has been maintained at 2 percentage points in both directions around the inflation target, the same as the previous years.' The agreed 5% target is used; the Inflation Report interim targets are not.

KR.wording: Price stability target from 2019 set by the Monetary Policy Board on 26 Dec 2018, in consultation with the Government: 2% in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index ('2019년 이후 물가안정목표'를 소비자물가 상승률(전년 동기 대비) 기준 2.0%로 확정 의결), the same level as the 2016–2018 target; the three-year application period is abolished (no fixed period), with the operation of the target reviewed every two years ('3년마다 재설정했던 물가안정목표의 적용기간을 없앴다. 다만, 2년 주기로 물가안정목표 운영 개선에 필요한 사항을 점검키로 했다').

CO.wording: Board of Directors, 25 Nov 2022: 'La Junta Directiva del Banco de la República reitera la meta de inflación del 3%' ('The Board of Directors of Banco de la República reiterates the 3% inflation target'); 'Las acciones de política monetaria están encaminadas a conducir la inflación a la meta del 3%, velando por la sostenibilidad de la actividad económica' ('Monetary policy actions are aimed at pushing inflation to the 3% target, while ensuring that economic activity is sustainable'). The release restates no range (the previous year's decision had kept a 2–4% range). The Banco de la República's page sits behind a bot check; its text was read from the site's print rendering and its date is confirmed by a same-day report quoting it.

This objective has also been clarified to note that MPC should discount disturbances to inflation that are expected to be temporary in a manner consistent with meeting the medium-term target'; 'The Reserve Bank will also continue to assess the impact of its monetary policy decisions on the Government's objective of supporting sustainable house prices as part of a redrafted context section' (Minister's release; value unchanged, the 2 percent mid-point of the 1–3 percent range; recorded because the remit is replaced).
